title: Naval 专题 · 长期游戏：健康、关系与人生选择
title_en: Naval Series · The Long Game: Health, Relationships and Life Choices

questions.question: 按这篇对 Naval「长期游戏」的拆解，在哪种情形下这套复利与信任的逻辑最容易失灵？
options: 老搭档之间握手就成事，连合同都不细读
一步就赚够、换行业从零开始，或底盘被战争毁掉
只和少数人深交，不去广泛结识浅层的关系
合作双方都愿意原谅对方偶尔的失误，彼此留了余地
questions.explanation: 长期游戏要求对手不走、规则不变、桌子不塌：一票就能赚够的人会背叛，换行业人脉信用带不过去，底盘被毁复利就断。留原谅的余地、握手成事、深交少数人，都是他说长期游戏顺利运转时的样子。
questions.question_en: Per this breakdown of Naval's 'long-term games', when does the logic of compounding and trust most readily break down?
options_en: When longtime partners close deals on a handshake without reading contracts
When one move pays enough, switching fields resets you, or war wrecks the base
When you go deep with a few people rather than collecting many shallow ties
When both partners are willing to forgive each other's occasional mistakes
questions.explanation_en: Long-term games need the other player to stay, the rules to hold and the table not to collapse: someone who can win enough in one move will defect, switching industries leaves your network and credibility behind, and a destroyed base breaks the compounding. Forgiveness, handshake deals and a few deep ties are what the game looks like when it works.

questions.question: 这篇认为 Naval 把钱、健康、平静和家串起来的那条链上，哪一环最弱？
options: 把自己的健康排在家庭之前，这与他的复利逻辑相互矛盾
说讲道德长期有回报，却又承认短期内不讲道德更划算
把「充满爱的家」当成独自能挣来的，忽略了家是退不出去的双人游戏
主张在有截止的时间框里反复试伴侣、工作和城市
questions.explanation: 他说心平静、钱赚到了，好关系自然会来，这等于把双人游戏当成单人游戏；他自己的长期游戏理论恰恰说复利要靠对方也留在桌边，而「吵一次就结束」放到有了孩子、退不出去的家里未必行得通。身体那一环反而被说成最扎实。
questions.question_en: This piece argues one link is weakest in the chain Naval draws from money to health, calm and family. Which?
options_en: Ranking his own health above family, which contradicts his own logic of compounding
Saying ethics pays off long-term while admitting unethical behavior pays in the short run
Treating a loving home as something you can earn alone, ignoring that it's a two-player game you can't exit
Advising people to iterate on partner, work and city within a fixed time frame
questions.explanation_en: He says that with a calm mind and money made, good relationships will follow — treating a two-player game as single-player. His own long-term-games theory says compounding needs the other side to stay at the table, and 'one fight and it's over' may not work in a family with kids you can't walk away from. The body link, by contrast, is called the most solid.

questions.question: 按 Naval 对「退休」的定义，下面哪个人才算已经退休了？
options: 已经不上班了，却每天熬夜盯盘、为未来回报苦撑的人
仍在全力投入新公司，但不再为想象中的明天牺牲今天的人
六十五岁领到养老金停止工作，却天天为将来焦虑的人
被动收入刚好覆盖开销，仍为下一次升职咬牙忍耐的人
questions.explanation: 他把退休定义为不再为某个想象中的明天牺牲今天，今天本身就完整了；按这个定义退休和停止工作无关。他自己 2026 年说只算「最低限度地退休」，却比以往投入更多精力在新公司上。
questions.question_en: By Naval's definition of retirement, which of these people is actually retired?
options_en: Someone no longer employed who stays up nightly watching markets, grinding for future returns
Someone pouring everything into a new company but no longer sacrificing today for an imagined tomorrow
Someone who stopped working at 65 on a pension yet worries about the future every day
Someone whose passive income just covers expenses but still grits their teeth for the next promotion
questions.explanation_en: He defines retirement as no longer sacrificing today for some imaginary tomorrow — when today is complete in itself. On that definition retirement has nothing to do with stopping work; in 2026 he called himself only 'minimally retired' while putting more energy than ever into a new company.
